title: Signposting in Academic Writing
text:
Effective academic writing depends heavily on signposting, the use of linking adverbials that guide readers through an argument. Words such as 'however', 'consequently' and 'furthermore' indicate whether a writer is contrasting ideas, drawing a conclusion or adding support. Nevertheless, writers who rely on these devices too heavily often produce prose that feels mechanical. Readers, in turn, tend to notice when such markers are absent, because the logical relationships between sentences become harder to follow.

For this reason, many style guides recommend using signposting selectively rather than in every sentence. A well-placed 'in contrast' or 'as a result' can clarify a complex point, whereas a string of identical connectors can distract the reader. Ultimately, the goal is not to display vocabulary but to make the structure of the argument transparent. Consequently, a skilled writer chooses each connector with care.

questions.text: According to the first paragraph, what do words such as 'however' and 'consequently' indicate?
options: How ideas in the text are logically related
The intended audience of the text

questions.text: What does the second paragraph say many style guides recommend?
Why would a reader probably find a text without signposting harder to follow?
options: Because the text would contain no argument
Because the logical links between sentences would be unclear
Because all of its sentences would be very short
Because the author would have used too many examples

questions.text: What can be inferred about a writer who repeats the same connector throughout a text?
options: They have a strong command of varied vocabulary
They risk distracting the reader from the structure of their argument
They are following the advice of most style guides
They have made the argument easier to understand

vocabulary.definition: the use of words or phrases that show the reader how a text is organised
done in an automatic way, without thought or feeling
only in certain cases, rather than always
easy to see through or understand; clearly shown

paragraph_translations: A escrita acadêmica eficaz depende muito da sinalização discursiva, ou seja, do uso de conectores que orientam o leitor ao longo de um argumento. Palavras como 'however', 'consequently' e 'furthermore' indicam se o autor está contrastando ideias, tirando uma conclusão ou acrescentando apoio. No entanto, autores que dependem demais desses recursos costumam produzir textos com aspecto mecânico. Os leitores, por sua vez, tendem a perceber quando esses marcadores estão ausentes, pois as relações lógicas entre as frases ficam mais difíceis de acompanhar.

Por essa razão, muitos guias de estilo recomendam usar a sinalização discursiva de forma seletiva, e não em todas as frases. Um conector bem colocado, como 'in contrast' ou 'as a result', pode esclarecer um ponto complexo, ao passo que uma sequência de conectores idênticos pode distrair o leitor. Em última análise, o objetivo não é exibir vocabulário, mas tornar a estrutura do argumento transparente. Portanto, um escritor habilidoso escolhe cada conector com cuidado.
